subject: geography

items.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
items.correct: They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.
items.misconception: Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
items.random_wrong: Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
items.why: Wind doesn't create hurricanes — warm ocean does. They draw energy from latent heat of evaporating seawater; that's why they weaken rapidly over land or cool water.

items.q: Tropical cyclones require sea surface temperatures above:
items.why: The answer examiners want is: 26.5 degrees C. “16.5 degrees C” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: Typhoon Haiyan storm surge at Tacloban reached:
items.why: Correct answer: 7 m. “2 m” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: Hurricane Katrina (2005) economic damage in $ billion:
items.why: The real figure is 125. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
